Like 2026-09-23 14:30. Several photos get one second apart, in the order picked.
%1$s could not be changed. Only photos found in the last check can be changed.
Instagram and KakaoTalk show photos in the order they arrived on the phone, not the date taken. iPhone photos arrive all at once, so the order gets shuffled.

They are not deleted but kept in the trash for 30 days. Until then \"Undo\" on the first screen puts everything back. Only when storage is short are originals deleted at once, and you\'re told beforehand.

Restoring an original from the Gallery trash by hand puts it next to the re-saved copy. To go back, always use \"Undo\" on the first screen. If it already happened, delete the restored originals again.
About as much as the photos being fixed, for a short while. The check result shows the storage needed. If there isn\'t enough, originals are deleted at once and can\'t be undone.
Will Google Photos upload them twice?
Usually not. Re-saved photos are identical to the originals, so they count as the same photos. If you still see some twice, turn off sync in the Gallery app. Google Photos backup can stay on.
The Gallery looks the same after fixing
That\'s normal. The Gallery already sorts by the date taken, so it looks the same before and after. What changes is the photo picker in apps like Instagram and KakaoTalk.
When a photo you re-dated in the Gallery jumps to the top in KakaoTalk, or shows as \"Today\" in Instagram. The button appears in the check result.
